Russian strikes killed at least 15 people in Ukraine’s Zaporizhzhia region, Ukrainian officials said Saturday, a day after U.S. President Donald Trump announced a deal to buy Russian diesel that Kyiv warned would help bankroll Moscow’s war in Ukraine.
Three children were among those killed when Russian aerial bombs hit residential buildings in Zaporizhzhia, Ukraine’s State Emergency Service said Saturday. At least 16 people were wounded in the attack.
Russia and Ukraine are locked in a long-range aerial war while their armies remain largely deadlocked on the front line, more than 4 1/2 years since Moscow’s full-scale invasion. Ukraine is struggling to counter escalating Russian bombardments that have killed more than 60 people over the past four days.
Trump said Friday he had struck a deal to obtain diesel from Russia, a stunning reversal of years of U.S. pressure on Moscow over its war with Ukraine and an attempt to address high fuel prices ahead of the U.S. midterm elections.
Russia to supply more than 300,000 tons of diesel to U.S. and global market, Trump says
Anger in Kyiv over diesel deal

He said the attacks show Moscow understands “any easing of pressure to mean they can keep fighting, to mean they can keep dropping bombs on cities,“ adding that “different signals are needed.”
Zelensky said Ukraine was preparing meetings and coordinating steps to counter the extra revenue Russia will receive from the diesel deal. In a post on X, he said he had discussed the developments with Finnish President Alexander Stubb, and said that Ukraine would receive ammunition in the coming days for the F-16s it uses to intercept Shahed drones.
“It is important to continue working together to protect people and limit Russia’s ability to wage this terrible war,” Zelensky said.
Trump had been set to discuss a suspected case of plague in Russia with President Vladimir Putin in a phone call.

corpus.title: Russian Strikes Kill At Least 17 In Zaporizhzhya, Disrupt Power In Kyiv, Officials Say
corpus.signal_text:
Russian strikes on Ukraine killed at least 17 people, including three children, in the southeastern city of Zaporizhzhya and disrupted electricity and water supplies in Kyiv on October 10, Ukrainian authorities said.
Rescue workers continued searching for survivors as Russia reported attacks on Ukrainian energy facilities.
The death toll from the morning Russian attack on Zaporizhzhya currently stands at 17, with 16 others injured, Ivan Fedorov, co-chair of the regional defense council, said on Telegram. Search-and-rescue operations were continuing, with six people still unaccounted for, he added.
Authorities have declared October 11 a day of mourning in Zaporizhzhya.
Rescuers pulled a woman alive from the rubble of a destroyed building and were taking her to hospital, the acting head of the regional military administration, Mykhaylo Semikin, said.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said as many as 12 people could still be trapped under the rubble.
Ukrainian authorities shared images of what they said was the aftermath of the attack, including badly damaged residential buildings.
The State Emergency Service said a Russian aerial bomb destroyed an entire entrance section of an apartment building and damaged other buildings and private homes. Rescuers extinguished a fire and continued searching through the rubble for possible survivors, it said.
Zaporizhzhya has been a regular target of Russian aerial strikes, with attacks intensifying in the past few months.
Russian attacks also caused widespread disruption in Kyiv. DTEK, Ukraine’s largest private energy provider, reported “new large-scale power outages” in the capital on October 10.
Local authorities said damage to an energy facility in the Kyiv region had worsened the capital’s electricity supply, causing interruptions to water supplies and temporarily halting metro services.
Trains subsequently resumed running on all metro lines, but with longer intervals between services, according to the Kyiv city administration. Authorities said repair crews were working to restore water supplies.
A Russian strike on a boat station in Kyiv's northern Obolon district also injured at least five people, Ukraine's State Emergency Service said.
The Ukrainian Air Force said Russia launched 160 attack drones against the country overnight, including 110 jet-powered Shahed drones.

corpus.title: Russian attacks kill 11 in Ukraine after Trump strikes diesel deal with Putin
corpus.signal_text:
Russian strikes killed at least 11 people in Ukraine’s Zaporizhzhia region, officials said on Saturday (October 10, 2026), a day after U.S. President Donald Trump announced a deal to buy Russian diesel that Kyiv warned would help bankroll Moscow’s war in Ukraine.
Three children were among the 11 people killed when Russian aerial bombs hit residential buildings in Zaporizhzhia, Mykhailo Semikin, head of the regional military administration, said on Saturday. At least 16 people were wounded in the attack, according to Ivan Fedorov, co-chair of the region’s defence council.
Russia and Ukraine are locked in a long-range aerial war, while their armies remain largely deadlocked on the front line, more than 4.5 years since Moscow’s full-scale invasion. Ukraine is struggling to counter escalating Russian bombardments that have killed more than 60 people over the past four days.
The latest attacks came a day after Mr. Trump said he had struck a deal to obtain diesel from Russia, a sharp reversal of years of U.S. pressure on Moscow over its war with Ukraine, and an attempt to address high fuel prices ahead of the U.S. midterm elections.
Mr. Trump said on social media on Friday (October 9, 2026) that he struck the deal with Russian President Vladimir Putin in a phone call in which he had been expected to discuss a suspected case of plague in Russia. Instead, Mr. Trump announced that Russia would immediately supply more than 300,000 tonnes of diesel, followed by an additional 500,000 tonnes in November 2026, and 1 million tonnes “immediately thereafter.” Russia would deliver an additional 3 million tonnes “within a short period of time” after that, he wrote.
Mr. Trump’s announcement was in stark contrast to a sweeping Russia sanctions law he signed last month, which aimed to clamp down on the oil and gas revenues that fuel Russia’s war against Ukraine.
In a lengthy post online reacting to the deal, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Russia would repay it “with further terror and perfidy.” He described it as an investment in the war, allowing it to be prolonged. “It plays into Russia’s hands — allowing it to kill more, wage war for longer, have even less respect for America, and inflict even greater losses and damage on the world,” he said.
According to a statement released by the Ukrainian Embassy in Washington, Mr. Zelenskyy called it “a weak decision, unfortunately, a weak decision by strong partners.”
